title: Commercial Acceptance & Privileged Onboarding Handoff
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Recording: https://redwood.ai/recordings/ff-20271102-7b9c.mp3

Summary: quick vendor intake to align commercial acceptance criteria, discuss MSA/DPA redlines, privileged access controls for the pilot Dedicated environment, and next steps for pricing approvals. Customer asked for KMS/HSM detail, audit log retention, and canary SLA.

Topics: commercial acceptance checklist; MSA redline path; DPA/data residency; Dedicated trial provisioning; SSO/KMS/HSM; pricing governance and internal approver timeline.

Action items (captured verbally in call): see below.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I think we said 45 but we'll take up to an hour — quick intros and then jump into the redlines and the pilot ask.
[00:15] Priya (Procurement): Hi, Priya here. We have Liam from legal and Marco from security, Anika is on for technical. Main ask is to get clear acceptance criteria so we can move this through finance next week.
[00:28] Liam (Legal): Hi all. We tried to pre-read the MSA you sent, a few sections that we want clarified — indemnity, subprocessing, and a couple of DPA points.
[00:38] Maya: Great, thanks. Evan's here so we can rattle through the tech stuff. Evan, you want to say hi?
[00:44] Evan (SE): Hey folks, Evan. I'll take the tech bits — KMS, network, and the Dedicated pilot provisioning.
[00:51] Dr. Anika: Quick note, Sable is a healthcare data controller in EU and US; data residency and auditability are hard blockers for the pilot.
[01:02] Maya: Understood. Ok, commercial acceptance — Priya, can you run through what procurement needs?
[01:10] Priya: Sure. We need: signed MSA with redline path, DPA aligned to EU GDPR and HIPAA carve-outs if needed, SLA uptime numbers for the Dedicated pilot, pricing approval thresholds, and evidence of SOC 2 Type II and pen test summary. Also, who has privileged access, and how is key material handled.
[01:29] Maya: Perfect. On the SOC2 and pen test, we'll share our SOC2 report and the executive summary of the most recent pentest — link I will drop after the call. For SLAs, we have canary options: hosted with 99.5% and Dedicated with 99.9+ committed in reserved capacity contracts.
[01:46] Marco (Security): When you say "KMS" — are you offering customer-managed keys in Dedicated or bringing-your-own-key (BYOK) for Private? We need HSM-backed keys or at least an HSM integration.
[01:57] Evan: For Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS through our KMS integration — in the Private deployment we can do BYOK and HSM. In Dedicated we can integrate with your cloud KMS (e.g., AWS KMS with grant flow) or use our KMS with tenant-specific key encryption. HSM-level attestation is available in the Private on-prem package.
[02:20] Liam: Is that in the MSA or a separate security annex? Our procurement folks like contract language that locks in key control obligations.
[02:29] Maya: We can add a security addendum referencing key controls; Evan can draft the technical appendix for the DPA/Security Schedule.
[02:36] Evan: I'll put in specifics: key rotation cadence, who has access to key material, KMS policy links, and HSM attestations where applicable.
[02:44] Dr. Anika: Also need KV cache behavior spelled out — we can't have PHI persisted in a non-isolated cache between customers.
[02:53] Evan: Right — we have tenant-isolated KV cache for Dedicated and Private; for hosted we offer strict TTLs and optional prefix caching. I'll note the default TTLs and the option to disable caching for PII workloads in the tech appendix.
[03:10] Priya: Pricing approval path — we have a pricing committee that needs the committed month and expected run-rate. Can you provide committed capacity pricing and overage rates? Also, break out unit economics per 1k tokens for the pilot workload.
[03:22] Maya: Yes, I'll share a pricing sheet. For Dedicated pilots we can offer a temporary committed rate for 90 days, after which we convert to monthly reserved pricing. I'll include per-token math and underwriting notes.
[03:33] Liam: On MSA redlines — we have one substantive ask: limitation of liability cap needs to be reciprocal and higher for security breaches. Also, data breach notification timelines — 72 hours is our baseline.
[03:45] Maya: We typically mirror industry standards; we can accept a reciprocal cap with carveouts for gross negligence. For notification we'll aim for 48-72 hours depending on the severity — Evan, is there an ops SLA for incident notifications?
[03:56] Evan: Yes, we have incident response playbooks. For Dedicated customers, we commit to an internal notification within 24 hours and customer notification within 48 hours for severity-1 incidents; lower severities follow our standard IR timeline. We'll include the IR appendix.
[04:14] Marco: Audit logs — retention and exportability are critical. We need 1 year of immutable logs for privileged actions, and the ability to export to our SIEM. Is that configurable?
[04:25] Evan: Logs are configurable per deployment tier. Dedicated supports 1+ years retention and direct export via syslog or push to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog). We'll document export formats and schema.
[04:37] Priya: For legal review speed, would you accept a redline in Word or do you prefer comments? Liam prefers a redline we can iterate on.
[04:46] Liam: A redline is preferred. Also, can you confirm insurance coverage — cyber liability limits?
[04:54] Maya: We have cyber liability limits in our MSA — I'll surface the current policy summary and carrier details.
[05:02] Dr. Anika: On the technical side, pilot scope: We want to run a 2-week Dedicated trial with production-like traffic (burst profile included). We'll measure p50/p95 latency, token cost per response, and end-to-end reliability including failover to another region.
[05:18] Evan: For the pilot we can provision a dedicated pool and enable tracing for the test period. We'll also run a small benchmark harness — p95 latency with your sample prompts and typical seq lengths. We should sync on the prompt corpus and the traffic profile.
[05:31] Priya: Timeline-wise, procurement needs final commercial terms by 2027-11-10 to get sponsor approval. Is that realistic?
[05:38] Maya: Tight but doable — if we get the redline today or tomorrow, legal-to-legal turnaround could be 3 business days. Pricing approval sheet I'll send today.
[05:47] Liam: We may have one more DPA ask around subprocessors — could you list all subprocessors and data flow?
[05:54] Evan: Yes, we'll provide a subprocessors list and an architecture diagram. Note that for Dedicated the subprocessors are minimal if you host in your VPC — for hosted there are more cloud services involved.
[06:07] Marco: Control plane access: who can see customer prompt text in the control plane, and do we have role-based access controls that restrict that to a small set of ops?
[06:17] Evan: Control plane access is RBAC-enabled; only specific roles get visibility into raw transcripts. For Dedicated we can restrict access to your designated tenant admins and our support engineers under a strict access policy and SSO with just-in-time access.
[06:33] Priya: Who signs the SLA in the MSA — is the SLA part of the MSA or a separate SOW?
[06:40] Maya: Typically SLA is an exhibit to the MSA — we can include the Dedicated SLA as an exhibit and have the SOW note committed capacity and pricing.
[06:47] Liam: We will run the MSA and DPA against our standard playbooks — expect redlines on indemnities and subprocessors.
[06:55] Maya: That's fine. I'll propose to push a clean MSA with an editable security addendum so you can iterate.
[07:02] Dr. Anika: Technical quick question — does Redwood support private endpoints into our VPC so data egress is controlled?
[07:10] Evan: Yes, Private deployment supports VPC peering and private endpoints. For Dedicated we can configure private connectivity or a transit gateway depending on your cloud topology.
[07:22] Priya: Any export controls or data transfer clauses we should be aware of for EU/US cross-border?
[07:29] Maya: We'll include standard SCCs for EU transfers and note our transfer mechanisms; for highly regulated data we recommend Private (on-prem) or VPC-backed Dedicated to limit cross-border flows.
[07:40] Liam: On the procurement checklist — what's the minimal signature set to start a pilot? Do we need full MSA or can we do a pilot SOW with acceptance terms and a temporary NDA?
[07:51] Maya: We can do a pilot SOW plus an abbreviated MSA addendum that covers liability and data handling for the pilot. Many customers start with that to unblock engineering quickly, then finalize full MSA during pilot.
[08:05] Priya: That helps. For approvals, CFO wants a clear exit clause for the pilot and an estimate of run-rate after pilot.
[08:13] Maya: We'll include an exit clause in the pilot SOW and provide a projected 12-month run-rate based on your expected throughput.
[08:21] Marco: One more security note — we require background checks for any vendor staff that will have privileged access to our Dedicated tenants. Is that part of your process?
[08:31] Maya: We do role-based OPS access with background checks for on-call staff who would escalate to production access; we will document the staff security screening procedures and provide named contacts for escalations.
[08:44] Evan: Also, for privileged access we support just-in-time access and session recording for escalations so you get an auditable trail.
[08:54] Priya: Great. Any competitors we should be aware of in your pitch?
[09:00] Maya: We've seen evaluation against Anthropic and OpenAI in similar RFPs; main differentiator is the Dedicated/Private options and predictable economics.
[09:09] Liam: Noted.
[09:12] Maya: Recap and next steps — I'll summarize:
  - Maya: Send pricing sheet, pilot SOW template, and redline-friendly MSA clean copy by end of day (link to drop).
  - Evan: Draft security appendix with KMS/HSM, KV cache settings, log retention/export schema, subprocessors list, and architecture diagram by 2027-11-04.
  - Priya/Liam: Return redline to MSA and DPA by 2027-11-05 if possible.
  - Maya: Provisioning request for Dedicated pilot: need sample prompts and traffic profile from Anika by 2027-11-03.

[09:48] Priya: Sounds good. We will aim for those dates; procurement needs the final pricing to route to the pricing committee on 2027-11-10.
[09:56] Maya: Perfect — I'll also attach SOC2 and the pentest exec summary.
[10:03] Dr. Anika: I'll send the sample prompt corpus and a traffic histogram (burst profile) after this call.
[10:09] Marco: We'll expect the subprocessors list and JIT access documentation.
[10:15] Maya: Super. Any final Qs?
[10:18] Liam: One admin question — can you provide a crm deal id for our internal tracker?
[10:23] Maya: Sure, the CRM deal id is RDW-2027-1123-SH.
[10:28] Priya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up by email with any minor clarifications.
[10:33] Maya: Thanks all, talk soon.

End of transcript.

Customer to return MSA/DPA redlines by 2027-11-05
